title: What If You Wore a Blindfold for Five Days Straight?

scenes.text: What if you wore a blindfold for five days straight? Your brain would start doing something odd.
In a 2008 study, forty-seven sighted adults took part. Half were blindfolded around the clock for five days.
By the end, their visual cortex, the part of the brain that handles sight, lit up when they used touch.
They also got better at reading Braille.
When researchers briefly disrupted that brain area with a magnetic pulse, their Braille reading got worse.
Within about a day of removing the blindfolds, the effect faded. Your brain rewires fast, and rewires back.
